2026-12-06.title: Second Sunday of Advent
readings: Comfort, O comfort my people; prepare the way of the Lord
Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation
We wait for new heavens and a new earth
Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight
2026-12-06.verse: He proclaimed, “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the thong of his sandals. I have baptized you with water; but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
theo: Isaiah 40 opens the “Book of Consolation”. After decades of exile God speaks tenderly: “Comfort, O comfort my people… Speak tenderly to Jerusalem.” The punishment is over; a road is to be built in the desert for God to lead his people home; valleys raised, mountains lowered. And the God who comes is a Shepherd who “will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom”.

Mark begins his Gospel with no birth story. Its first words are a title: “The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” Then he quotes Isaiah and Malachi, and John the Baptist appears in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. People come from all Judea and Jerusalem, confessing their sins. John points away from himself: “The one who is more powerful than I is coming… he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

Peter's letter explains the delay of the Lord's return: “with the Lord one day is like a thousand years… The Lord is not slow about his promise… but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.” God's patience is time given for conversion. So: “Since you are waiting for these, strive to be found by him at peace, without spot or blemish.” Advent is the time to straighten the crooked road of our hearts.
conn: Scholars call Isaiah 40–55 the Book of Consolation, addressed to the exiles in Babylon (6th century BC). Its first word in Hebrew, nahamu, “comfort”, is doubled for emphasis.
Ancient kings had roads levelled before their visits. Isaiah pictures a royal highway built for God himself to lead the exiles home.
“The beginning of the good news” echoes Genesis 1:1, “In the beginning”. The Gospel is a new creation.
Mark 1:6 says John wore camel's hair and a leather belt, exactly like Elijah (2 Kings 1:8). The reader is meant to see Elijah returning before the Lord's day (Malachi 4:5).
Untying a master's sandals was a slave's task; rabbinic tradition said a disciple should do everything for his teacher except that. John says he is unworthy even of the slave's task.
A thousand years as one day.
2 Peter 3:8 quotes Psalm 90:4. God's time is not ours; his delay is mercy.
altar: At the beginning of Mass we say: “I confess to almighty God…” As at the Jordan, the people of God come confessing their sins and preparing the way.
John baptised with water; Christ baptises with the Holy Spirit. In the Eucharist the Spirit is called down (the epiclesis) upon the gifts and upon us, so that we may become one body.

fathers: “Prepare the way of the Lord within your hearts… The way we prepare for the Lord is a way within, in the heart.”
He explains that the valleys filled are the humble raised, and the mountains brought low are the proud humbled.

2026-12-06.prayer: Almighty and merciful God, may no earthly undertaking hinder those who set out in haste to meet your Son, but may our learning of heavenly wisdom gain us admittance to his company. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Repentance prepares the road for the Lord.
John points away from himself to Christ.

2026-12-06.special: Second Sunday of Advent, Year B. Colour: violet.
illus: Before a bishop's visit to a Kerala parish, the road to the church is repaired, potholes filled, branches cut back, arches put up. We do all that for a bishop. What road are we preparing for Christ?

family.explain: John the Baptist told people to get ready for Jesus by saying sorry for their sins. We get ready the same way: by Confession and by being kind.
family.intention: We pray for courage to say sorry to God and to one another.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we clean up in our hearts and our home this week?”

kidsaint: A governor who became bishop of Milan by surprise, when a child in the crowd shouted, “Ambrose for bishop!” He later baptised St Augustine. Lesson: God can call us when we least expect it.
term: Greek for a “change of mind”: turning the whole person back to God. It is the first word of John's and Jesus' preaching.

pm.open: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God. Lord, as we gather on this Second Sunday of Advent, prepare the way in our hearts for your Son. Amen.
share: Isaiah cries: prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). What mountain of pride or valley of discouragement needs levelling in me?
Peter says God is patient, not wanting any to perish (2 Peter 3:9). How have I experienced God's patience?
John the Baptist called people to confess their sins (Mark 1:5). When will I go to confession this Advent?
pm.resp: Prepare the way of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like John the Baptist she may prepare the way of the Lord.
For those who need comfort, that they may hear God's tender voice.
For sinners, that they may turn to God this Advent.
For our country, that justice and peace may be found on its paths.
For our families, that we may prepare our hearts more than our houses.
pm.close: Lord God, you speak tenderly to your people. Level the mountains of our pride, fill the valleys of our discouragement, and make straight the path for your Son. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the prophet Isaiah begins with a beautiful word: “Comfort, O comfort my people.” After years of exile, God's first word is not anger but tenderness.

And then a voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord.” Every valley lifted up, every mountain made low. In ancient times roads were repaired before a king's visit. Isaiah says: God himself is coming; prepare his road!

Mark begins his Gospel with John the Baptist in the desert. People come from everywhere, confessing their sins and being baptised in the Jordan. That is how the road is prepared: not with decorations but with repentance.

What are the mountains in us? Pride, stubbornness, the refusal to forgive. What are the valleys? Discouragement, laziness, the feeling that I can never change. Advent asks us to bring both to God. Confession is the bulldozer that levels the road!
And John points away from himself: “One more powerful than I is coming… he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” A true Christian is like John: a finger pointing to Jesus.

St Peter tells us why the Lord seems to delay: “The Lord is not slow about his promise, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish.” This Advent is God's patience with us. Let us not waste it. Make a good Confession. Comfort someone who is low. And prepare the road for the King.
kids: Children, when an important guest is coming, what do we do? We clean the house!
John the Baptist told the people: Jesus is coming; clean your hearts!
How do we clean our hearts? By saying sorry to God in Confession, and sorry to people we have hurt.
This week, say sorry to someone and make them smile!
